subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the batik technique, which material is used as the resist to block out areas of fabric?
questions.explain: Batik is a wax-resist dyeing method in which hot wax prevents dye from reaching the covered areas.

questions.q: In screen printing, how is the ink transferred onto the fabric?
options: Pushed through a mesh screen with a squeegee
questions.explain: Screen printing forces ink through open areas of a mesh screen using a squeegee to print the design.

questions.q: Tie-dye is an example of which category of technique?
questions.explain: Tying or binding the fabric resists the dye, leaving undyed patterns where the fabric is bound.

questions.q: Which technique involves stitching smaller pieces of fabric onto a larger background fabric?
questions.explain: Appliqué attaches cut shapes of fabric onto a background, usually secured with stitching.

questions.q: Why is a wax resist applied before dyeing in batik?
options: To stop the dye reaching the covered areas of fabric
To make the dye spread more evenly
To speed up the drying of the dye
questions.explain: The wax seals the fibres so those areas stay their original colour when the fabric is dyed.

questions.q: Why is block printing well suited to creating a repeat pattern across a length of fabric?
options: The same carved block can be stamped again and again
It uses a computer to duplicate the image
It dyes the whole cloth a single colour
It weaves the pattern into the cloth
questions.explain: A single carved block can be inked and pressed repeatedly to build up an even repeating pattern.

questions.q: An artist wants a crisp, hard-edged geometric motif printed identically many times. Which stitching or print method fits best?
questions.explain: Screen printing reproduces sharp, consistent shapes repeatedly, making it ideal for hard-edged repeated motifs.

questions.q: Embroidery is best described as decorating fabric using which of the following?
questions.explain: Embroidery decorates a surface with stitches worked in thread using a needle.

questions.q: Which of the following is a natural fibre?
questions.explain: Cotton is a natural plant fibre, whereas polyester, nylon and acrylic are synthetic.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a mordant when dyeing textiles?
options: To fix the dye so it bonds to the fibres
To bleach the fabric before dyeing
questions.explain: A mordant helps the dye bind permanently to the fibres, improving colourfastness.

questions.q: In weaving, which threads are held taut lengthwise on the loom?
questions.explain: Warp threads run lengthwise and are held under tension on the loom while the weft is woven across them.

questions.q: Felting works by matting fibres together. Which combination of conditions causes wool to felt?
questions.explain: Warmth, moisture and repeated agitation cause the scales on wool fibres to interlock and mat together.

questions.q: Which of these is a synthetic (man-made) fibre?
questions.explain: Polyester is manufactured from petrochemicals, while linen, silk and wool are natural fibres.

questions.q: Why might a designer choose silk for a flowing, luxurious garment?
options: It is smooth and has a natural lustre and drape
It is stiff and holds sharp folds
It is coarse and highly textured
questions.explain: Silk's smooth surface gives it a sheen and soft drape well suited to fluid, luxurious garments.

questions.q: A student wants to create a raised, three-dimensional padded surface on their textile piece. Which process is most appropriate?
questions.explain: Quilting stitches layers of fabric with wadding between them, creating a raised, padded three-dimensional surface.

questions.q: A designer needs to add colour to cloth so that tightly folded and bound areas stay white. Which process achieves this?
questions.explain: Binding the fabric resists the dye, so the bound areas remain undyed while the rest takes colour.

questions.q: Which designer, central to the Arts and Crafts movement, is famous for textile and wallpaper patterns such as 'Strawberry Thief'?
questions.explain: William Morris led the Arts and Crafts movement and designed nature-based repeat patterns including 'Strawberry Thief'.

questions.q: Anni Albers is best known as a pioneering artist working in which textile discipline?
questions.explain: Anni Albers was a Bauhaus-trained weaver celebrated for her innovative woven textiles and writings on weaving.

questions.q: The American artist Faith Ringgold is especially known for creating which type of textile work?
questions.explain: Faith Ringgold combines painting, quilting and text to make narrative 'story quilts'.

questions.q: The artist Yinka Shonibare is known for using which distinctive material in his work?
questions.explain: Shonibare uses brightly patterned Dutch wax cotton to explore identity, colonialism and cultural exchange.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) Art & Design (J170) specification; Textile Design
